title: Balanced entropy forms of two fixed positive operators admit an exact scalar testing-measure transfer
status_authority: The exact source scope and version-bound receiving review are recorded below; this card does not certify priority, physical operation, or practical advantage.

proof_availability.classification_scope: For faithful positive A,X on the same finite-dimensional space, with no commutation assumption, the positive measure mu=h'' of h(t)=Tr(A-tX)_+ represents the positive and negative traces of every real pencil alpha A+beta X by the scalar densities alpha r+beta against mu. Consequently, for nonnegative mixture coefficients alpha_j,beta_j and real c_j satisfying both sum_j c_j alpha_j=0 and sum_j c_j beta_j=0, the balanced entropy combination of the mixtures equals its scalar integral against mu. Every scalar inequality of this balanced form, with optional linear trace terms, holds for all such operator pairs iff it holds for all nonnegative scalar pairs. Singular finite matrices follow by the stated epsilon-identity regularization and entropy continuity. Boundary: Does not cover three or more independent sources, arbitrary products or log-Euclidean means, partial transposes, general matrix-valued functional calculus inequalities, or unbalanced entropy combinations. The testing measure is abstract and does not represent one physical measurement.

title: A binary-input channel has the same fixed-prior Umegaki SDPI constant with any finite quantum reference
status_authority: The exact source scope and version-bound receiving review are recorded below; this card does not certify priority, physical operation, or practical advantage.
reported_status: The recipient checked the selected source passages and the cited published ingredient at the exact scope below. No full-package audit, separate binary producer audit, producer-script replay, external priority review, or physical/practical validation is asserted.

proof_availability.classification_scope: For every finite-output classical channel T with binary input and every full-support fixed prior pi, let K=A_0+A_1, Y_y=T_{y0}A_0+T_{y1}A_1, and q_y=(T pi)_y. For arbitrary positive A_0,A_1 on any common finite-dimensional quantum reference, sum_{y:q_y>0} D(Y_y || q_y K) <= eta(T,pi) sum_{i=0}^1 D(A_i || pi_i K), where eta(T,pi) is the scalar fixed-prior Umegaki SDPI constant. Scalar references give the matching lower bound, so allowing an arbitrary finite quantum reference does not change this fixed-prior constant. Boundary: This fixes the binary transmitted alphabet and the prior. It is not the global-prior binary coefficient in N970, not an arbitrary-alphabet theorem with arbitrary references, not a reduction of multi-symbol quantum-memory problems, and not a t log t matrix-SDPI separation.

title: A qubit trine obstructs a universal three-source balanced entropy transfer
status_authority: The exact source scope and version-bound receiving review are recorded below; this card does not certify priority, physical operation, or practical advantage.
reported_status: The recipient checked the selected trine and scalar-entropy source passages at the exact scope below. No full-package audit, separate binary producer audit, producer-script replay, external priority review, or physical/practical validation is asserted.

proof_availability.classification_scope: The scalar balanced third finite difference s(a+b+c)-s(a+b)-s(a+c)-s(b+c)+s(a)+s(b)+s(c), for s(t)=-t log t, is nonnegative for all a,b,c>=0. For the three real qubit trine projectors P_0,P_1,P_2, the corresponding balanced matrix trace-entropy expression is (3/2)log(3/4)<0, since the sum has spectrum (3/2,3/2), each pair has spectrum (3/2,1/2), and each individual projector has spectrum (1,0). The scalar-to-matrix transfer therefore fails in this explicit three-source case, and negativity persists under sufficiently small positive epsilon-identity perturbations. Boundary: This is an obstruction to one universal balanced three-source entropy lift. It is not a W3 counterexample, does not contradict the older arbitrary-classical-channel/qubit-reference global mutual-information theorem, and does not establish a t log t fixed-prior matrix-SDPI separation.
